row.evidence: Spotfire's admin docs say Spotfire Server can synchronize users, groups and group memberships using the SCIM standard APIs and that SCIM is enabled by default; Spotfire publishes no prices and directs pricing questions to a contact form.
row.notes: Quote-only: spotfire.com/pricing returns 404 and the site sends pricing questions to a contact-us form; Cloud Software Group sells Spotfire only as annual/multi-year subscriptions (licences: Industry Pro, Analytics, Analysis Consumer, Analysis Viewer). SCIM 2.0 is built into self-hosted Spotfire Server (11.5+, on by default) at /spotfire/api/rest/scim/v2/<domain>, authenticated with OAuth2 client tokens from register-api-client/issue-access-token. Docs name Okta and Azure as intended SCIM clients; the Okta catalogue app is SWA only. Users created over SCIM cannot be edited or deleted in the admin UI. Login uses OpenID Connect, LDAP, Kerberos or X.509 (no SAML page found). The webstore (buy.spotfire.com) was unreachable.

auth.token_source: Spotfire Server CLI: register-api-client with scopes user-directory.read.all and user-directory.write.all, then OAuth2 grant (authorization code for Okta) or issue-access-token

deprovision.data_retained: SCIM 'active' sets the user's administrative status; a disabled Spotfire account cannot log in but its record is kept. DELETE /Users/:Id removes the user.
deprovision.notes: Docs do not state which call Okta/Entra send on unassignment or what DELETE does to library content.

filtering.notes: Operators eq, co, sw, ew, AND, OR.

roles.how: No roles attribute; licences and licence features are assigned to Spotfire groups, so SCIM-pushed group membership controls access.

limitations.text: Users, groups and memberships created over SCIM cannot be updated or deleted from the Spotfire Server admin UI.
Spotfire stores a single email per user (the primary one), though SCIM defines emails as multi-valued.
Bulk is not supported (per the ServiceProviderConfig example in Spotfire's community article).
SCIM is a feature of self-hosted Spotfire Server 11.5 or later; the admin must register an OAuth2 API client on the server.

user_api.notes: Spotfire Server exposes OAuth2-secured public REST APIs (browsable in Swagger UI on the customer's server), but no non-SCIM user-management endpoints were found in the public docs; user CLI commands (create-user, delete-user, enable-user) exist but are not an API.

okta.notes: OIN page ticks only SWA; no SCIM or provisioning ticks. Spotfire's docs say to create a SCIM-compliant app in Okta and point it at the generic endpoint.

fallbacks.other_sync: LDAP / Active Directory user and group synchronization; external authentication providers (OpenID Connect)
